_comment: Real-landscape validation manifest (cosmo plan Phase 6 / §5b).
Small, TRACKED file. Names the DEM to fetch and where the authoritative
per-sample regression targets come from. NO large data is ever committed.
The DEM is fetched keyless via the lsdtt-fetch-raster CLI (Copernicus
GLO-30 on AWS / Microsoft Planetary Computer -- NO API key), clipped to the
bounding box below into a temporary workdir by
tests/scripts/run_cosmo_validation.py, and deleted after the run.
Regression targets are HARVESTED from OCTOPUS (v2.3) via WFS -- see
octopus_source below and the sample-table header for full provenance.
description: Dethier et al. (2014) Front Range 10Be basins. Pilot subset = a compact Boulder Creek / Front Range cluster of 14 small catchments (0.07-10.11 km2) deliberately spanning 1962-3480 m elevation, to (a) shake out the harness on a single modest DEM and (b) expose the elevation-dependent residual (see caveat below) before GB-scale Himalayan datasets.

published_reference.citation: Dethier, D.P., Ouimet, W., Bierman, P.R., Rood, D.H., Balco, G. (2014), Geology 42(2), 167-170.
published_reference.calculator: OCTOPUS v2.3 recalculation with CAIRN (Mudd et al. 2016; github LSDTopoTools_CRNBasinwide), default Stone/Lal 'St' scaling (EBE_* fields).

_comment: Regression targets (concentration, uncertainty, standard, denudation rate)
are harvested from OCTOPUS, NOT scraped from the paper and NOT invented.
OCTOPUS recalculates every rate with CAIRN -- the same algorithm
lsdtt-cosmo-tool implements -- so these are a NEAR-CAIRN oracle, not
bit-exact (see residual_expectation).
octopus_source.cql_note: Filter with CQL_FILTER, not bbox: the OCTOPUS server throws a ProjectionException on the WFS 2.0.0 bbox parameter.
octopus_source.scaling_scheme: St (Stone/Lal) -- EBE_MMKYR / EBE_GCMYR. OCTOPUS also stores EBEL/EBELNS (LSDn). Run lsdtt-cosmo-tool in the matching St scheme for a like-for-like compare; confirm the scheme flag at run time.

_comment: Simon 2026-07-24: agreement will NOT be exact. lsdtt3 has diverged from
stock CAIRN -- updated production-rate parameters, plus a high-elevation
production-scaling fix THIS suite found (the S_tot>=1 clamp defect, plan
§9b findings log). The residual is expected to be ELEVATION-DEPENDENT.
residual_expectation.band: measured-then-frozen on the FIRST accepted network run; do NOT assert a tight zero-residual band. Record elevation_ave_m per basin in the summary so the residual-vs-elevation trend is visible.
residual_expectation.attribute_residual_to: production-parameter divergence + high-elevation scaling scheme + DEM product (COP30 vs the SRTM used in the OCTOPUS recalculation) + basin pixel binning -- NOT to bugs.

dem.dem_source_note: Keyless. Driven through the lsdtt-fetch-raster CLI, which retrieves and clips Copernicus GLO-30 from AWS Open Data (dem_source: cop30_aws) or Microsoft Planetary Computer (dem_source: planetary_computer) with NO account or API key. Set dem_source to planetary_computer to use the PC STAC mirror instead.
dem.target_epsg_note: UTM 13N (EPSG:32613) for the Colorado Front Range; matches OCTOPUS PROJEPSGID for these S169 basins. The cosmo CLIs require a PROJECTED CRS, so the DEM is warped to UTM at fetch time.
dem.resolution_choice_note: COP30 (30 m) vs the DEM used in the OCTOPUS/CAIRN recalculation is a DOCUMENTED, attributable difference in the validation (DEM resolution + product), not a bug -- record it alongside the production-scheme residual in the summary.

bounding_box._comment: Union of the 14 pilot basins' OCTOPUS outline footprints, padded ~0.02 deg. Covers the whole cluster in one modest DEM.

_comment: lsdtt-cosmo-tool run knobs for this dataset. The default
threshold_contributing_pixels (1000 = 0.9 km2 at 30 m) is TOO HIGH for
these sub-km2 Front Range catchments: it snaps small outlets onto a much
larger channel, inflating the basin and wrecking the comparison, and skips
basins that never reach 1000 px. Lowered here so small basins delineate
near their true size. Basins below ~this*cellsize remain unreliable (outlet
snap cannot resolve a catchment smaller than the threshold) and are flagged
in the summary; that is a delineation limit, not a numeric bug.
